summary: Revision 1 slice 1: added the optional boolean `focusSheen` field to ZestCustomProps (off by default, no new export or plumbing) and the CSS focus streak in the shared stylesheet. A regular opted-in button gets one `::after` band clipped by its existing rounded overflow; an opted-in split control gets one whole-control overlay on the split wrapper, keyed to :has(:focus-visible), clipped by its own radius so neither segment's focus ring is cut, and with the chevron mount streak suppressed for that control. The band is a 45-degree gradient travelling top-right to bottom-left over 0.6s, uses currentColor on regular buttons and style+variant+forced-theme markers on split controls, ends transparent, keeps the label above it, and is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Wrote focused behavioural and characterisation tests, and documented the option in documentation/api.md, documentation/features.md, documentation/examples.md and the new docs/features/zest-button-focus-sheen/guide.md. README.md and documentation/configuration.md are left for the other slice as instructed. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build and the full npm test suite (26 suites, 331 tests, all passing). Finished slice 2 of revision 1 (R1, A4). README.md gained a focus-streak key-feature bullet and an 'Opt-in Keyboard Focus Streak' section with regular and split examples that links the new guide. documentation/configuration.md gained a 'Focus Streak Defaults' section plus TOC entry, showing how the provider's defaultProps sets focusSheen app-wide and how a single button opts out. Extended the A4 coverage in __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx to assert the configuration page (defaultProps, reduced motion, guide link) and the README (focusSheen, dropdownOptions, guide link). Verified the slice-1 artifacts (focusSheen prop, focus-streak CSS, focus-sheen and characterization tests, guide, api/features/examples docs) are present and untouched. All checks run: tsc typecheck, focused jest (32/32), npm run build, and full npm test (26 suites, 332 tests pass).

tests.name: R1: focusSheen is off by default and opts in per button without leaking
R1: focusSheen={false} renders no streak layer
R1: turning focusSheen off at runtime removes the streak layer from a regular button and a split control
R1: a split button opts in with one whole-control layer and no per-segment layer
R1: opting in leaves the accessible name, role and pressed state alone
R2: plain focus or a mouse click adds no JS state; only :focus-visible starts the sweep
R2: each focus arrival plays exactly one sweep and a re-focus replays it
R2: the existing focus ring remains the primary focus signal
R2: a toggle in its on state keeps its pressed look and focus ring while the streak plays
R3: the band is a 45-degree diagonal that travels top-right to bottom-left over 0.6 seconds
R3: the band is clipped by the button's rounded overflow and never changes its layout
R3: the band ends transparent and is not left stuck or tinted
R3: very small and very large buttons share one continuous sweep with no stacked layers
R4: every style, variant and forced theme gets the streak layer on a regular button
R4: every style, variant and forced theme gets the whole-control layer on a split button
R4: the band colour follows currentColor and the button's own theme tokens so it reads on every style
R4: the label sits above the translucent band so it stays readable
R5: a split control plays one whole-control sweep from either segment
R5: the split band is clipped to the rounded outer corners without clipping either focus ring
R5: the open menu is rendered outside the clipping wrapper and stays visible
R5: moving focus from the main segment to the chevron keeps one overlay for the whole visit
A1: reduced motion disables the focus streak for regular and split buttons
A1: without the preference the streak keeps its animation on both button kinds
A2: an opted-in split control suppresses the chevron mount streak
A2: a split control that is not opted in keeps its chevron mount streak
A4: the API, features and examples pages document focusSheen for regular and split buttons
A3: a plain regular button keeps its current wrapper element, classes and DOM
A3: a split wrapper and its two segments keep their current classes and gain no sheen classes
A3: the existing focus-ring rule is still the focus indicator
A3: the existing chevron mount-streak rule and keyframes are unchanged
A3: a button that does not opt in keeps its click behaviour and adds no extra elements
A4: the configuration page sets focusSheen app-wide through defaultProps and the README links the guide
